notice: General preparedness guidance summarized from official publications. It is not an instruction for a current incident. During an emergency, the instructions of your local authorities always take priority.

guides.title: Earthquakes
guides.scope: United States federal guidance; useful as general reference elsewhere.
before: Practise how to protect yourself (Drop, Cover and Hold On) with family and coworkers.
Sign up for earthquake alerts where they are available.
Make a family emergency communications plan with an out-of-area contact and a place to meet if separated.
Make a supply kit with food and water for several days, a flashlight, a fire extinguisher and a whistle.
Secure heavy items such as bookcases, refrigerators and televisions.
during: Protect yourself right away: Drop, Cover and Hold On.
If you are inside, stay inside; do not run outside and avoid doorways.
If you are in bed, turn face down and cover your head and neck with a pillow.
If you are driving, pull over, stop and set the parking brake.
If you are outside, stay outside and move away from buildings, trees, streetlights and power lines.
after: Expect aftershocks and be ready to Drop, Cover and Hold On again.
If you are in a damaged building, go outside and move away; do not enter damaged buildings.
If you are trapped, text or bang on a pipe or wall; use a whistle instead of shouting and cover your mouth.
In a tsunami area, go inland or to higher ground as soon as the shaking stops.
Watch for damaged buildings, gas and water leaks and downed power lines; wear protective clothing during cleanup.

guides.title: Tsunamis
guides.scope: United States federal guidance; useful as general reference elsewhere.
before: Learn the natural signs: an earthquake, a loud roar from the ocean, a sudden rise or wall of water, or water draining to expose the sea floor.
Know and practise your community's evacuation plans and routes from home, work and places you visit.
Pick refuges at least 100 feet (about 30 m) above sea level or at least one mile (about 1.6 km) inland.
Make a family emergency communication plan and sign up for local warnings.
during: If an earthquake happens, protect yourself from the shaking first (Drop, Cover and Hold On).
When the shaking stops, if there are natural signs or official warnings, move immediately as high and as far inland as possible — do not wait for an evacuation order.
Leave immediately if told to do so; evacuation routes are often marked with a wave and an arrow.
If you are in the water, grab something that floats. If you are in a boat, face the waves and head out to sea; if you are in a harbour, go inland.
after: Listen to local authorities for areas to avoid and shelter locations.
Avoid wading in floodwater, which may be deeper than it looks and contain dangerous debris.
Beware of electrocution from underground or downed power lines.
Stay away from damaged buildings, roads and bridges; use text messages to save phone lines for emergencies.

guides.title: Floods and flash floods
guides.scope: United States federal guidance; useful as general reference elsewhere.
before: Know whether you live in a flood-prone area and how you would receive local warnings.
Plan where you would go and how you would get there if told to evacuate.
Keep important documents in a waterproof place or as protected digital copies.
Gather supplies, including medication, for everyone in the household and for pets.
during: Find safe shelter right away; evacuate immediately if told to do so and never drive around barricades.
Do not walk, swim or drive through flood water — six inches (15 cm) of moving water can knock you down and one foot (30 cm) can sweep a vehicle away.
Stay off bridges over fast-moving water.
If trapped in a building, go to the highest level; do not climb into a closed attic. Only go on the roof if necessary and signal for help.
If your car is trapped in rapidly moving water, stay inside; get on the roof if water rises inside the car.
after: Listen to local authorities before returning home.
Stay out of flood water, which can be contaminated and hide debris.
Do not touch electrical equipment if it is wet or if you are standing in water.
Use generators only outdoors and away from windows; wear protective clothing when cleaning up.

guides.title: อุทกภัย / น้ำท่วม
guides.authority: กรมป้องกันและบรรเทาสาธารณภัย (ปภ.) กระทรวงมหาดไทย
guides.scope: คำแนะนำสำหรับประชาชนในประเทศไทย
before: เตรียมถุงยังชีพที่มีของใช้จำเป็นให้ใช้ได้อย่างน้อย 3–5 วัน เช่น อาหาร น้ำ ยารักษาโรค และตรวจสอบให้พร้อมใช้อยู่เสมอ
เก็บเอกสารสำคัญ (เช่น สำเนาทะเบียนบ้าน) ในถุงพลาสติกหรือซองกันน้ำ
เตรียมวัสดุที่ลอยน้ำได้ เช่น ยางในรถยนต์ แกลลอนน้ำ ไว้ใช้ยึดเกาะพยุงตัว และวางไว้ในจุดที่หยิบติดตัวได้ทันทีเมื่อต้องอพยพ
ติดตามพยากรณ์อากาศ ประกาศเตือนภัย และระดับน้ำในพื้นที่ แล้วปฏิบัติตามคำเตือนอย่างเคร่งครัด
กำจัดขยะที่อุดตันท่อและทางระบายน้ำรอบบ้าน
during: ตัดกระแสไฟฟ้าโดยปิดสวิตช์และสับคัตเอาท์ ห้ามใช้หรือสัมผัสเครื่องใช้ไฟฟ้าขณะตัวเปียกหรือยืนบนพื้นเปียก
ถ้าต้องอพยพ ให้ช่วยเด็กและผู้สูงอายุก่อน และทำตามแผนอพยพไปยังที่ปลอดภัย
อย่าอพยพไปตามเส้นทางที่เป็นทางไหลของน้ำ และหลีกเลี่ยงการเดินข้ามลำน้ำที่สูงเกินเข่าหรือไหลเชี่ยว
ห้ามขับรถยนต์หรือรถจักรยานยนต์ผ่านบริเวณที่น้ำท่วมสูง
สวมรองเท้าบูทเมื่อเดินลุยน้ำ ใช้ไม้สำรวจเส้นทาง และไม่เดินลุยน้ำตอนกลางคืน
after: ระวังอันตรายจากไฟฟ้า สัตว์มีพิษที่อาจหนีน้ำเข้ามาในบ้าน และเศษแก้วหรือของมีคมที่จมอยู่ใต้น้ำ
ระวังโรคที่มากับน้ำท่วม
ติดตามประกาศของหน่วยงานในพื้นที่ก่อนกลับเข้าบ้าน

guides.title: Hurricanes, typhoons and tropical cyclones
guides.scope: United States federal guidance; useful as general reference elsewhere.
before: Know whether you live in an evacuation zone; learn the routes, practise with your household and pets, and decide where you will stay.
Follow the instructions of local emergency managers as the threat develops.
Prepare your home for high winds and flooding: clear drains and gutters and trim damaged tree limbs.
during: Pay attention to emergency information and alerts; if you are told to evacuate, do so immediately.
For high winds, take refuge in a designated storm shelter or an interior room.
If trapped by flooding, go to the highest level of the building; do not climb into a closed attic.
Do not walk, swim or drive through flood water.
after: Follow local officials' information and special instructions.
Do not touch wet electrical equipment; turn off power at the main breaker only if it is safe to do so.
Do not wade in flood water, which can contain pathogens, chemicals, debris and live wires.
Wear protective clothing and work with someone else during cleanup; children should not help with cleanup.

guides.title: Thunderstorms, lightning and hail
guides.scope: United States federal guidance; useful as general reference elsewhere.
before: Know your area's risk; thunderstorms can happen at any time of year and any hour.
Sign up for your community's warning system.
Identify sturdy buildings close to where you live, work, study and play.
Trim trees that could fall on your home and secure outdoor furniture.
during: When thunder roars, go indoors — a sturdy building is the safest place.
Pay attention to weather reports and warnings and be ready to change plans.
Avoid running water and landline phones; electricity can travel through plumbing and phone lines.
Unplug chargers and appliances to protect them from surges.
after: Follow authorities and forecasts to know when it is safe to go outside.
Watch for fallen power lines and trees and report them immediately.
Be alert for flash flooding.

guides.title: Tornadoes
guides.scope: United States federal guidance; useful as general reference elsewhere.
before: Know the signs: a rotating funnel-shaped cloud, an approaching cloud of debris, or a loud roar like a freight train.
Sign up for your community's warning system and pay attention to weather reports.
Identify and practise going to a safe shelter for high winds, such as a safe room or storm shelter; otherwise a small, interior, windowless room on the lowest level of a sturdy building.
during: Go immediately to the safe location you identified.
Protect your head and neck with your arms and put materials such as furniture and blankets around you.
Do not stay in mobile homes or modular structures when a tornado threatens.
Keep listening for current emergency information and instructions.
after: Keep listening to local authorities for updated information.
If trapped, cover your mouth with cloth to avoid breathing dust; text, bang on a pipe or use a whistle instead of shouting.
Stay clear of fallen power lines and broken utility lines.

guides.title: Wildfires
guides.scope: United States federal guidance; useful as general reference elsewhere.
before: Set up defence zones around your home and property.
Remove gas, oil, propane and other fuel sources from within 30 feet (about 9 m) of your home.
Stay informed about weather conditions and other emergencies that may cause a wildfire.
during: Evacuate immediately once a notice has been issued so that your route is not blocked by the fire.
Follow the instructions of local authorities.
after: Return only when authorities say it is safe.
Protect your breathing where air quality is poor because of smoke.

guides.title: Volcanic eruptions
guides.scope: United States federal guidance; useful as general reference elsewhere.
before: Know your area's risk from volcanic eruption.
Ask local emergency management about evacuation and shelter plans and protection from ash.
Sign up for volcano activity notifications where available.
Keep non-perishable food, cleaning supplies, water and medication for several days.
during: Listen to alerts and follow evacuation orders from local authorities; evacuate early.
Avoid areas downwind and river valleys downstream of the volcano.
If you have enough supplies, shelter from ash where you are: cover ventilation openings and seal doors and windows.
after: Follow authorities to learn whether it is safe to return.
Avoid driving in heavy ash; it can clog engines and stall vehicles.
Avoid contact with ash if you have breathing problems.

guides.title: Landslides and mudslides
guides.scope: United States federal guidance; useful as general reference elsewhere.
before: Know the landslide risk in your area; ask officials whether a landslide map exists.
Learn the warning signs: new cracks or bulges in ground or pavement, soil moving away from foundations, tilting structures, broken water lines.
Know your community's evacuation plans and sign up for local warnings.
during: If you are under a landslide warning, evacuate early.
Move away from the path of a landslide or debris flow as quickly as possible.
Avoid river valleys, low-lying areas, the bases of steep slopes and narrow canyons.
Listen for unusual sounds such as trees cracking or boulders knocking together.
after: Stay away from the slide area; more material may come loose.
Watch for flooding, which can follow a landslide.
Listen to authorities about when it is safe to return; report downed power lines.

guides.title: Extreme heat
guides.scope: United States federal guidance; useful as general reference elsewhere.
before: Find places with air conditioning that you can go to.
Prepare your home to keep heat out, for example with shades that block the sun.
Check that family members and friends have a plan to stay cool.
during: Stay in an air-conditioned place if possible.
Avoid strenuous activities and drink fluids.
Wear lightweight, light-coloured, loose clothing.
Watch for heat illness; very high body temperature, hot dry skin, confusion or unconsciousness can be a medical emergency — call your local emergency number.
after: Check on neighbours, especially older adults and young children.
Keep following local heat advisories until they are lifted.

guides.title: Extreme cold and winter storms
guides.scope: United States federal guidance; useful as general reference elsewhere.
before: Prepare your home to keep out the cold with insulation, caulking and weather stripping; learn how to keep pipes from freezing.
Install and test smoke alarms and carbon monoxide detectors with battery backups.
Pay attention to weather reports and sign up for local warnings.
Include warm clothing and blankets in your supplies.
during: Stay off roads if at all possible; if trapped in your car, stay inside.
Stay indoors and dress warmly.
Use generators and grills only outdoors and away from windows; never heat your home with a gas stove or oven.
Watch for signs of frostbite (loss of feeling and colour) and hypothermia.
after: If someone shows signs of hypothermia, go to a warm room and warm the centre of the body first; keep the person dry and wrapped in blankets.
Take refuge with family or friends if your home loses power or heat for more than a few hours.

unavailable.reason: No complete official before/during/after guidance was reviewed yet.
